sentences.en: Humans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason.
sentences.zh: 人对噪声非常敏感，这是有充分理由的。

sentences.en: From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger.
sentences.zh: 从演化的角度看，声音提供了至关重要的信息，帮助我们在周围环境中辨别方向、避开危险。

sentences.en: To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them.
sentences.zh: 为帮助我们对响亮或突如其来的声音给予应有的注意，体内的化学活动会随之发生变化。

sentences.en: Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight.
sentences.zh: 我们的血压会上升，肌肉会绷紧，腺体还会释放激素，使我们做好战斗或逃跑的准备。

sentences.en: In the short term, this is a good thing.
sentences.zh: 从短期来看，这是件好事。

sentences.en: When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.
sentences.zh: 可是，长期处在过多的噪声中，这些反应就可能导致众多健康问题，从睡眠受干扰，甚至到心血管疾病。

sentences.en: The World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night.
sentences.zh: 世界卫生组织最近将过量噪声认定为对公共健康“被低估的威胁”。该组织还指出，孟买、东京、布宜诺斯艾利斯等城市居民夜间承受的噪声，远高于建议的40分贝。

sentences.en: A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health.
sentences.zh: 欧洲环境署的一份报告认为，噪声在欧洲是个长期而普遍的问题。至少每五人中就有一人经常暴露在被认为有害健康的噪声水平下。

sentences.en: 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.
sentences.zh: “没有什么‘耳睑’能挡住噪声、保护大脑，”声学顾问尼克·安东尼奥说。他参与过英国及国际噪声标准的制定。

sentences.en: The good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，已有好几座城市在努力降低噪声。

sentences.en: One of the first to do so was London.
sentences.zh: 伦敦便是最早这么做的城市之一。

sentences.en: 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio.
sentences.zh: “他们就如何让公交车更安静提出建议，减少道路噪声，也控制飞机噪声，因而成功让城市安静了一些，”安东尼奥说。

sentences.en: Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound.
sentences.zh: 还有些城市采用了降噪路面涂层，同时配以能减弱声音的绿化植被。

sentences.en: Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier.
sentences.zh: 还有些措施针对的是更具体的问题：华盛顿特区对汽油动力吹叶机的禁令最近已生效；而在纽约市，一项已获通过的法规规定，对改装车辆使其噪声增大的人处以罚款。

sentences.en: 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says.
sentences.zh: 安东尼奥说：“人们正在亲眼看到，城市环境变安静给自己带来了哪些好处。”

sentences.en: 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'
sentences.zh: “我预计，今后这样的做法会越来越多。”

sentences.en: Researchers are also seeking to understand what aspects of silent experiences are most beneficial to our health.
sentences.zh: 研究者也在设法弄清，体验安静时，究竟哪些方面对健康最有益。

sentences.en: One of the best-researched is the flotation tank: a lightproof, soundproof tank of salt water in which a person floats as a form of deep relaxation.
sentences.zh: 其中研究最为充分的一种是漂浮舱：它是一种装有盐水、既遮光又隔音的舱体，人躺在水中漂浮，以获得深度放松。

sentences.en: While some people experience altered perception in the tanks, involving subtle humming sounds and visual effects, these effects are benign and do not detract from the benefits of the experience, says Justin Feinstein, a clinical neuropsychologist.
sentences.zh: 有些人在舱中会感到知觉发生变化，比如听到轻微的嗡鸣声或出现某些视觉感受；临床神经心理学家贾斯廷·范斯坦说，这些现象是良性的，并不会削弱这种体验的益处。

sentences.en: 'When you don't have external sensory stimuli coming in, the brain tries to fill the void to make sense of this dark and silent world,' he explains.
sentences.zh: 他解释说：“没有外部感官刺激传入时，大脑会试图填补这种空缺，以理解这个既黑暗又寂静的世界。”

sentences.en: 'In these tanks, some people can even hear the sound of their eyes blinking,' says Feinstein.
sentences.zh: 范斯坦说：“在这些漂浮舱里，有些人甚至听得到自己眨眼的声音。”

sentences.en: 'But it is the ability to focus on the breath that helps people reach a relaxed or meditative state.'
sentences.zh: “不过，真正有助于人们进入放松或冥想状态的，是能够把注意力集中在呼吸上。”

sentences.en: To further explore flotation tanks as a therapeutic tool, Feinstein and his colleagues recruited 50 people with a variety of conditions related to stress and had them answer a questionnaire prior to and following a flotation session.
sentences.zh: 为了进一步探究漂浮舱的治疗用途，范斯坦和同事招募了50名患有不同压力相关病症的人，让他们在一次漂浮体验之前和之后各填一份问卷。

sentences.en: Participants reported decreases in muscle tension, pain and symptoms of their conditions after a single, 1-hour float, alongside an increase in feelings of relaxation and overall wellbeing.
sentences.zh: 参与者表示，只漂浮一次、持续一小时后，自己的肌肉紧张、疼痛和原有病症的症状都有所减轻，同时感觉更加放松，整体幸福感也有所提升。

sentences.en: Less is known about what effects sensory deprivation can have on the brain.
sentences.zh: 感官剥夺究竟会怎样影响大脑，人们知道的就少一些。

sentences.en: To investigate, Feinstein's team had 48 people participate in either three 90-minute float sessions or three 90-minute periods of relaxing on a chair which reclined.
sentences.zh: 为研究这个问题，范斯坦的团队让48人参加两种活动之一：要么漂浮三次，每次90分钟；要么在可向后倾斜的椅子上放松三次，每次也是90分钟。

sentences.en: Participants had their brains scanned using functional magnetic resonance imaging at the beginning and end of the trial.
sentences.zh: 试验开始和结束时，研究者都用功能性磁共振成像技术扫描了参与者的大脑。

sentences.en: Float sessions uniquely decreased activity in the default mode network (DMN), a collection of brain regions commonly linked with depression.
sentences.zh: 只有漂浮体验降低了默认模式网络（DMN）的活动水平。这个网络由一组脑区构成，通常被认为与抑郁有关。

sentences.en: Feinstein says it is an exciting finding, because flotation tanks seem to offer a way of 'resetting' our nervous system to prevent it from getting out of balance.
sentences.zh: 范斯坦说，这一发现令人振奋，因为漂浮舱似乎能为“重置”神经系统提供一种途径，防止它失去平衡。

sentences.en: Neurobiologist Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan is also an advocate of silence as a therapy.
sentences.zh: 神经生物学家泰·多坦·本-苏桑也主张把安静用作一种治疗手段。

sentences.en: 'When we find ways to be quiet, we are not only quiet in our environment, but quiet in our inner selves,' she explains.
sentences.zh: 她解释说：“当我们找到让自己安静下来的办法时，静下来的不只是周围的环境，还有我们的内心。”

sentences.en: 'This allows us to be more aware of what is happening around us and what the situation may require from us so we can provide [a more] adequate response.'
sentences.zh: “这样我们就能更清楚地觉察周围正在发生什么，也更清楚眼前的情形可能需要我们做什么，从而作出［更为］恰当的回应。”

sentences.en: Not everyone will benefit from silence to the same extent, but Ben-Soussan says one characteristic is key: the person must need to want to engage in the experience.
sentences.zh: 安静给每个人带来的好处不尽相同，但本-苏桑认为有一点至关重要：这个人自己必须愿意投入这种体验。

sentences.en: 'We see from animal models and human studies that volition and intentionality is important,' she says.
sentences.zh: 她说：“动物模型和人体研究都让我们看到，自主意愿和明确的意向很重要。”

sentences.en: 'When people do not want silence, it can be very distressing.'
sentences.zh: “如果一个人并不想要安静，安静反而可能让他非常难受。”

sentences.en: Eric Pfeifer, a psychotherapy researcher, also concedes that some people may not benefit from silence, particularly those who are in a heightened state of stress.
sentences.zh: 心理治疗研究者埃里克·普法伊费尔也承认，有些人可能无法从安静中受益，尤其是那些正承受较强压力的人。

sentences.en: 'People in these states may not be able to relax or calm down in a silent condition,' he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“在这些状态下，人即使身处安静的环境，也未必能够放松或平静下来。”

sentences.en: Professional guidance can be useful, he adds, allowing people to approach silence slowly so that they can gradually enjoy the benefits.
sentences.zh: 他补充说，专业指导会有帮助，能让人循序渐进地接触安静，渐渐享受到它的益处。

sentences.en: And Pfeifer is convinced that silence is more attainable in everyday life than people think.
sentences.zh: 普法伊费尔确信，在日常生活中获得安静，比人们以为的更容易。

sentences.en: First, complete silence isn't necessary.
sentences.zh: 首先，并不一定得完全无声。

sentences.en: In a recent study, he found that participants reported more relaxation and less boredom when they sat quietly in an outdoor garden compared with a completely silent room.
sentences.zh: 他在最近的一项研究中发现，与坐在完全无声的房间里相比，参与者静坐在露天花园时，自述感觉更放松、也没那么无聊。

sentences.en: Second, Pfeifer believes we don't need a lot of silence to gain benefits.
sentences.zh: 其次，普法伊费尔认为，我们不必长时间保持安静也能从中受益。

sentences.en: 'You don't need to spend hours in silence,' he says.
sentences.zh: 他说：“你用不着一连好几个小时都静着。”

sentences.en: 'It is likely better to have more frequency of silence for a few minutes at a time than a longer period of silence only once a week.
sentences.zh: “多找几次安静的时刻，每次只需几分钟，效果很可能比一周只静一次、但一次静很久更好。

sentences.en: Just finding those places in your daily life where you can find some silence ... can make a big difference.'
sentences.zh: 只要在日常生活中找到一些能享受片刻安静的地方……就可能产生很不一样的效果。”
